idiom_name: pqxx::work scoped transaction + outbox row + relay
implementation_notes: C++ has no transaction manager, so the atomic unit of work is a database transaction plus the message as an outbox row: with libpqxx a pqxx::work commits on tx.commit() and aborts in its destructor otherwise, and with sqlite3 an explicit BEGIN/COMMIT pair does the same; a relay then turns committed rows into real sends. RAII makes this safer than the C equivalent, but the relay, its acknowledgement handling and the retry policy are still hand-written. The classic broker-transaction structure is still justified when the business state and the message live in the same broker rather than in a database.
pitfalls: Forgetting tx.commit() aborts the whole unit of work silently at scope exit (the pqxx::work destructor rolls back), which hides the bug until a message goes missing.
libpqxx and sqlite3 connections and transactions are not thread-safe: keep one transaction on one thread and never let a relay share the connection inside the transaction.
Publishing from inside the transaction body can reach the broker before COMMIT, so a rollback still emits a message; publish only after the commit point.

variants.name: librdkafka transactional producer through its C++ API
variants.implementation_notes: The C++ wrapper exposes the same transaction state machine as the C library: RdKafka::Producer::init_transactions(), begin_transaction(), produce(), send_offsets_to_transaction() and commit_transaction()/abort_transaction(), with the completion events delivered through the polled queue. Use it for consume-transform-produce loops where offsets and records must commit together, or when the business state lives inside the cluster; the producer holds at most one transaction at a time and none of it spans a database.
pitfalls: A single producer instance can hold only one transaction at a time and the transactional producer is not thread-safe.
Transactions need Kafka 0.11+ brokers and a stable transactional.id, otherwise zombie fencing does not apply and a restarted producer can duplicate or be fenced by itself.
The polled event queue must be served or the transaction callbacks never fire and the commit appears to hang.
